test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statement accurately describes 'The War That Made R&AW' by Anusha Nandakumar and Sandeep Saket?

options.text: Detailed history of India's external intelligence and geopolitics
Memoir of a former R&AW agent
Critique of post-2000 domestic intelligence reforms

solution:
The correct answer is __**Detailed history of India's external intelligence and geopolitics**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The book titled **The War That Made R&AW** is authored by **Anusha Nandakumar** and **Sandeep Saket**. It provides a comprehensive and detailed account of the events surrounding the **1971 Indo-Pak War** and the clandestine role played by India's external intelligence agency. **Hence, statement 1 is correct.**

• The narrative centers on the visionary leadership of **Rameshwar Nath Kao** (R.N. Kao), the founding father and the first chief of the **Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW)**. It describes how he built the organization from its inception in **1968** into a formidable intelligence force.

• The book explores the **geopolitical** complexities of the **Cold War** era, the internal crisis in **East Pakistan**, and the strategic maneuvers by **India** to manage the influx of refugees and the eventual liberation of **Bangladesh**.

• It is a work of **non-fiction** based on historical research and archival data, rather than a fictional espionage thriller. **Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.**

• While the book focuses on the life and work of **R.N. Kao**, it is a historical narrative written by researchers/filmmakers and not a personal memoir written by a former agent. **Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.**

• The scope of the book is limited to the foundational years of the agency and the **1971** conflict; it does not address or critique domestic intelligence reforms that occurred after the **year 2000**. **Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW):** It was established on **September 21, 1968**, following the intelligence failures observed during the **Sino-Indian War of 1962** and the **Indo-Pakistani War of 1965**. Before its creation, external intelligence was handled by the **Intelligence Bureau (IB)**.

• **Organizational Structure:** R&AW is headquartered in **New Delhi** and reports directly to the **Prime Minister of India** through the **Cabinet Secretariat**. It is not subject to the same parliamentary oversight as other government departments to maintain operational **secrecy**.

• **The 1971 Context:** R&AW's most significant early success was **Operation Jackpot**, which involved providing arms, training, and intelligence support to the **Mukti Bahini**, the Bengali resistance movement in **East Pakistan**. This operation was pivotal in the surrender of **93,000 Pakistani soldiers** on **December 16, 1971**.

• **R.N. Kao:** Known as a **legendary spymaster**, Kao served as the chief of R&AW from its founding until **1977**. He also founded the **Aviation Research Centre (ARC)** and the **Special Frontier Force (SFF)**, which are integral parts of India's security apparatus.

• **Motto:** The official motto of R&AW is **Dharmo Rakshati Rakshitah**, which translates from **Sanskrit** to 'The Law protects when it is protected'.

• **Geopolitical Impact:** The events described in the book highlight the shift in **South Asian** power dynamics, where **India** established itself as a dominant regional power despite opposition from the **United States** and **China** during the conflict.

**Important Points__**

• The book is particularly noted for detailing the **covert operations** that took place months before the formal declaration of war, showcasing the importance of **intelligence-led warfare**.

• The authors, **Anusha Nandakumar** and **Sandeep Saket**, are also known for their work in the film industry, which contributes to the **narrative-driven** and engaging style of this historical account.

• The **1971 War** remains a landmark event in **Indian history**, and this book serves as a tribute to the unsung heroes of the **intelligence community** who worked behind the scenes to ensure national security.
</ul
